# Integration Guide

This guide walks through wiring the staged migration into the live website.
**Zero Hostinger login required** — `upload-config.php` is generated by CI from
GitHub Secrets, and the `uploads/` directory is auto-created by `upload.php` on
its first write. Until every step here is completed, the live site is
unaffected — the contents of this folder are dormant.

## Pre-flight checklist (before touching anything)

- [ ] You have access to the Supabase Dashboard for project `elrnafeyidalkswgdqvx` (to copy the JWT secret)
- [ ] You have **GitHub repo Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions** write access
- [ ] You can run Node 18+ locally and have this repo checked out
- [ ] Existing FTP secrets (`FTP_HOST`, `FTP_USERNAME`, `FTP_PASSWORD`, `FTP_REMOTE_DIR`) are already configured — the deploy workflow already uses them

## Step 1 — Move the new files into their final locations

From the repo root:

```bash
# PHP endpoint + reference template
cp hostinger-migration/public/upload.php public/upload.php
cp hostinger-migration/public/upload-config.example.php public/upload-config.example.php

# Config generator (runs in CI before the FTP step)
cp hostinger-migration/scripts/generate-upload-config.mjs scripts/generate-upload-config.mjs

# One-time bulk migration script
cp hostinger-migration/scripts/migrate-storage-to-hostinger.mjs scripts/migrate-storage-to-hostinger.mjs

# Rewritten hook (replaces the Supabase version)
cp hostinger-migration/src/hooks/useImageUpload.ts src/hooks/useImageUpload.ts
```

## Step 2 — Apply the patches to existing files

Three small additions are recorded in `integration-diffs/existing-files.patch`.
Apply them with:

```bash
git apply hostinger-migration/integration-diffs/existing-files.patch
```

This patch:

- **`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`** — inserts a new "Generate upload-config.php from secrets" step before the FTP step, and changes the FTP `exclude:` block from `**/.htaccess` to `**/uploads/**`.
- **`.gitignore`** — adds `uploads/`, `public/uploads/`, and `public/upload-config.php` (the generated file is built into `build/`, never committed).
- **`public/.htaccess`** — adds `Options -Indexes` and an explicit `upload.php` rewrite passthrough.

> **Heads-up on `.htaccess`:** the patch removes `**/.htaccess` from the FTP exclude block, so `public/.htaccess` will now flow on every deploy. If you have any tweaks made directly on the Hostinger server that are NOT in `public/.htaccess`, copy them into `public/.htaccess` first or they will be overwritten on the next push.

## Step 3 — Add GitHub Secrets

In **GitHub repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret**, add:

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` | Supabase Dashboard → Project Settings → API → "JWT Secret" (NOT the anon key) |
| `ADMIN_EMAILS` | Comma-separated lowercased admin emails, e.g. `admin@theciovision.com,owner@theciovision.com`. Must match the `email` claim in their Supabase JWT. Keep in sync with `public.admin_users`. |
| `MIGRATION_TOKEN` | Leave **empty** for now. You will set this to a long random hex string only during Step 6, then clear it again in Step 8. |

The `UPLOADS_URL` is hardcoded in the workflow to `https://theciovision.com/uploads`. If your domain ever changes, edit `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` directly.

## Step 4 — Verify locally

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit          # TypeScript still compiles
npm run build             # Vite build succeeds
```

You can also dry-run the generator locally if you want to see the output:

```bash
SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET=fake ADMIN_EMAILS=test@example.com UPLOADS_URL=https://theciovision.com/uploads \
  node scripts/generate-upload-config.mjs build
cat build/upload-config.php
```

(Then delete `build/upload-config.php` — it's harmless but contains a fake secret.)

## Step 5 — Commit + push (this deploys everything to Hostinger)

```bash
git add public/upload.php public/upload-config.example.php \
        scripts/generate-upload-config.mjs \
        scripts/migrate-storage-to-hostinger.mjs \
        src/hooks/useImageUpload.ts \
        public/.htaccess .gitignore .github/workflows/deploy.yml
git commit -m "Migrate image/PDF storage from Supabase to Hostinger"
git push origin main
```

GitHub Actions will:

1. Build the site
2. Generate `build/upload-config.php` from the secrets you added in Step 3
3. FTP-upload `build/` to Hostinger — including `upload.php`, `upload-config.php`, and the updated `.htaccess`

After ~3 minutes:

- `https://theciovision.com/upload.php` exists on the server and is configured
- `public_html/uploads/` does **not** exist yet, but the first upload will create it (see `upload.php:227`, `mkdir(..., 0755, true)`)

Smoke-test from the admin panel: log into the site as an admin and upload a new
image somewhere (e.g. a test case study). The saved URL should be
`https://theciovision.com/uploads/website-images/...` and the image should
render. If this works, the endpoint is live.

> **What's the live-site impact at this point?**
>
> - Public pages: zero. They read DB URLs that still point to Supabase.
> - Admin panel: new uploads start landing on Hostinger immediately. Existing rows still point to Supabase until Step 7.

## Step 6 — Set the migration token (temporary)

The bulk-migration script needs a way to call `upload.php` without a Supabase
JWT. It uses a one-time shared token.

1. Generate a random token locally: `openssl rand -hex 32` (or any 32+ char hex string)
2. In **GitHub Settings → Secrets → Actions**, update `MIGRATION_TOKEN` to that value
3. Push an empty commit (or re-run the deploy workflow manually) to redeploy with the token baked in:
   ```bash
   git commit --allow-empty -m "Enable migration token"
   git push origin main
   ```
4. Locally, add to `.env`:
   ```
   HOSTINGER_UPLOAD_URL=https://theciovision.com/upload.php
   HOSTINGER_MIGRATION_TOKEN=<the same long random string>
   ```

## Step 7 — Run the migration

**Dry-run first** (no side effects, confirms script can list all files in Supabase storage):

```bash
node scripts/migrate-storage-to-hostinger.mjs
```

**Upload-only pass** (copies every Supabase file to Hostinger, HEAD-verifies each, writes `migration-report.json`; no DB writes; live site still serving from Supabase):

```bash
node scripts/migrate-storage-to-hostinger.mjs --upload-only
```

Inspect `migration-report.json` — `uploadFailures` and `verifyFailures` should both be empty. Spot-check a few of the new URLs in a browser tab.

**Apply DB rewrites** (this is the moment the live site starts serving from Hostinger):

```bash
node scripts/migrate-storage-to-hostinger.mjs --apply
```

Pre-flight re-HEADs every URL. If anything fails, no DB writes happen and the script aborts. Otherwise it PATCHes every row. Pull up the public site and click through pages: magazines list, leadership page, case studies, articles. Every image and PDF should load from `theciovision.com/uploads/...`.

## Step 8 — Clear the migration token

1. In **GitHub Settings → Secrets → Actions**, set `MIGRATION_TOKEN` back to an empty string (or delete the secret — the generator defaults to empty when unset)
2. Push an empty commit (or re-run the deploy) so the new empty value is baked into `upload-config.php`:
   ```bash
   git commit --allow-empty -m "Clear migration token"
   git push origin main
   ```
3. Locally, remove `HOSTINGER_UPLOAD_URL` and `HOSTINGER_MIGRATION_TOKEN` from `.env`

## Step 9 — If anything looks wrong

See `ROLLBACK.md` for a full playbook organized by symptom. The fastest paths:

- **DB rewrites went wrong** → `node scripts/migrate-storage-to-hostinger.mjs --rollback` (≈30s, restores every changed row to its original Supabase URL)
- **Admin uploads fail** → fix the GitHub Secret, push an empty commit (≈3min)
- **Nuclear option** → `git revert <integration-commit>` + `git push` (≈3min, plus `--rollback` if `--apply` had run)

Supabase storage is untouched until Step 10, so every rollback path is non-destructive.

## Step 10 — Cleanup (do this only after a few days of confidence)

1. (Optional, after weeks of confidence) Empty the Supabase storage buckets `website-images` and `magazine-pdfs` via the Supabase dashboard to reclaim the storage quota.
2. (Optional follow-up PR) Drop the storage RLS policies in `supabase/migrations/20260405093000_secure_admin_access.sql` lines 132–164, since the buckets no longer hold data.
